item.description: by Anonymous You came in here already convinced you had won. That is the tell. All flash, all noise. Like the world exists to admire you. You do not hear the music anymore. item.title: What Wanders Through a Body?
item.description: At curious Portland gallery Lumber Room, corporeal works by Louise Bourgeois and Isabelle Albuquerque converse. by Lindsay Costello The myth of feminine hysteria didn’t start in a Victorian sanatorium. Long before Freud heard about it and thought it sounded super legit, ancient Greek doctors imagined the uterus as a restless “wandering womb,” traversing the body and wreaking emotional havoc.
